statement: A teacher hands out pencils from a box. If she gives each student $5$ pencils, she has $14$ pencils left over. If instead she gives $7$ pencils to every student except the last one, then the last student gets only $3$ pencils and the box is empty. How many pencils are in the box?

choices.misconception: I found the 9 students, but then multiplied by 5 and forgot the 14 pencils left over.
I ignored the last student being short and wrote 7s = 5s + 14, which gave 7 students and 49 pencils.
I found the 9 students and multiplied by 7, forgetting that the last student got only 3 pencils.
I found the 9 students, but then gave every one of them 7 pencils and added the last student's 3 on top: 7 × 9 + 3 = 66.

hints: Let $s$ be the number of students and count the pencils in two ways.
The first way gives $5s + 14$ pencils. The second gives $7(s - 1) + 3$ pencils.

solutions.reliable: Let there be $s$ students. Giving $5$ to each uses $5s$ pencils and leaves $14$, so the box has $5s + 14$ pencils. Giving $7$ to each of $s - 1$ students and $3$ to the last uses $7(s - 1) + 3 = 7s - 4$ pencils. So $5s + 14 = 7s - 4$, giving $s = 9$, and the box has $5 \cdot 9 + 14 = 59$ pencils. Check: $7 \cdot 8 + 3 = 59$.
solutions.elegant: If the last student had received a full $7$, the teacher would have needed $4$ more pencils. Going from $5$ each with $14$ to spare to $7$ each with $4$ missing, the extra $2$ pencils per student used up $14 + 4 = 18$ pencils. So there are $9$ students and $5 \cdot 9 + 14 = 59$ pencils.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
